name: inprocess-obi-tlul-timer-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches one real OpenTitan TL-UL register target in one process: the Earlgrey RV timer as a beat_to_tlul register target. Every case line states the A-channel handshake (opcode/address/mask/data) and the D-channel response (data/error) the target's own pins carried, and the summary states the target's protocol and bridge.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one TL-UL target at 0x40003000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter (the target profile's own protocol is tl-ul/1, address_width 32, data_width 32, integrity required, one outstanding).

The generic tlul_register_observe kernel is used: the pinned OpenTitan rv_timer RTL is driven through beat_to_tlul and its a_valid/a_ready/a_opcode/a_param/a_size/a_source/a_address/a_mask/a_data/a_user and d_valid/d_ready/d_opcode/d_param/d_size/d_source/d_sink/d_data/d_user/d_error are exposed as passive taps. The specialised tlul_timer kind is refused by name because its generated model exposes no passive protocol trace.

Window: the profile's own 4 KiB rv_timer window. Registers used here: CTRL(0x4, rw), COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118, rw). 0x40003000..0x40004000 does not overlap the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and clears the 4 GiB bound.

The target declares one interrupt output (timer.interrupts) but no behavior file, so it declares no F5 trigger/status facts: F5 is refused by name, the output is observed only, and the summary states target0_f5 no. A declaration that states the four F5 facts is now admitted for TL-UL after the real rv_timer F5 run (configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-tlul-timer-f5.json); this F2/F4 scenario still declares no behavior, so its own refusal is the missing-facts word unsupported-f5:target-irq-semantics:tl-ul:source_port,source_bit_offset,trigger_writes,status_offsets.
No DMA is declared, so F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL.
The profile declares 50 MHz, the same as the CPU, so one host tick drives both models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.
